description:
Here are the descriptions of the provided plots, following your guidelines:

The plots illustrate the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy, displaying three different accuracy metrics. Both the x and y-axes share the same labels and scales across all plots. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence", has a linear scale, ranges from 0.86 to 1.00, and has tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy", has a linear scale, ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, and has tick labels at intervals of 0.2. 

The first plot displays a light blue line with circular markers, representing "Δ Accuracy". This line begins at approximately 0.93 at an initial confidence of 0.86 and decreases to approximately 0.22 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The line shows a decline from 0.93 to 0.81 at an initial confidence of 0.89, then increases slightly to 0.84 at 0.91, and then declines again. Error bars are present at each data point.

The second plot displays an orange line with triangular markers, representing "Accuracy". This line begins at approximately 0.18 at an initial confidence of 0.86 and increases to approximately 0.24 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The line shows a general increasing trend, with a slight decrease between 0.94 and 0.96, where it goes from 0.22 to 0.19. Error bars are present at each data point.

The third plot displays a green line with square markers, representing "Initial Accuracy". This line begins at approximately 0.78 at an initial confidence of 0.86 and increases to approximately 0.88 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The line shows a steady increase from 0.78 to 0.82 at an initial confidence of 0.90, then a more gradual increase to 0.88. Error bars are present at each data point.
